title: Internal Load-Diffusion Doubler across the Fwd Cargo Door Surround Frames C38 to C42
abstract: A machined titanium doubler is proposed on the inner face of frames C38 to C42 to spread the corner load of the forward cargo door cut-out into the adjacent bays, answering repeat cracking on high-cycle MERIDIAN-46 aircraft.

sections.reason: Since late 2023, five operators have reported cracking in the lower forward corner of the forward cargo door cut-out on MERIDIAN-46 aircraft in cargo-heavy long-haul operation. Fourteen findings are recorded across a population of roughly 250 aircraft, the earliest at 18 400 flight cycles. Four findings exceeded the allowable damage limits of the applicable repair scheme and needed an engineering repair with a life limit attached. Cracking continued on aircraft that already carry the titanium corner fitting standard, which tells us the driver is the load path itself and not the fitting material.
sections.description: A machined Ti-6Al-4V doubler is installed on the inner face of the fuselage frames between stations C38 and C42, bridging the lower corner of the door cut-out and diffusing the corner load into the two adjacent frame bays. Peak stress at the cut-out radius is predicted to fall by 24 per cent. The frame doubler assembly D5321117326151 is replaced by the new machined item, the lower web D5321117734118 is retained and locally re-drilled, and the splice plate BEL987037-46 at station C40 is replaced by a thicker item. The joint is closed with titanium bolts AES495354-07 to the pattern of drawing D53211167819, with harness routing detail on D53211108423. Access is through the forward cargo compartment, zones 113 and 115, and across the door threshold in zone 891, with the lower shell lining removed between the two frames. The doubler footprint runs within 20 mm of the door warning wiring support bracket D9221132883400 and of the mounting for the forward door proximity sensor 3WT6; both clearances are open points.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 7.1 kg per aircraft, symmetric about the centre line, with a centre-of-gravity shift below 0.05 per cent MAC. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable with the pre-modification standard, because the frame drilling pattern changes and the doubler cannot be removed without replacing the frame web. Once a revised fatigue substantiation is issued, the repeat detailed visual inspection of the corner region can be withdrawn, which is the operator benefit. Maintenance, illustrated parts and repair content for ATA 53-21 will all need updating, and at least one in-service repair scheme occupies part of the area the doubler wants.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only at this stage. The provisional estimate is six days inside a scheduled C-check on the assumption that the cargo compartment is already open for other work. No production cut-in is proposed until the retrofit design is frozen and the freighter read-across has been assessed separately.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis has to confirm the clearance to the door warning wiring bracket and to the proximity sensor mounting, establish whether the existing corner skin repair scheme survives embodiment, and settle whether the modification can be offered to aircraft that have not had the titanium corner fitting standard applied.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.05 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in proposed at this stage
